import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from view import View

def test_basic():
    v = View()
    rid = v.begin('q1')
    assert rid == 1
    v.loading = False
    # finish with rid
    assert v.finish(rid, ['row1']) == True
    assert v.rows == ['row1']
    # second begin increments
    rid2 = v.begin('q2')
    assert rid2 == 2
    # finish with old rid should return False
    assert v.finish(rid, ['old']) == False
    # finish with new rid should succeed
    assert v.finish(rid2, ['row2']) == True
    assert v.rows == ['row2']

def test_duplicate_rid():
    v = View()
    rid1 = v.begin('q1')
    rid2 = v.begin('q2')
    # finish with rid1 twice
    assert v.finish(rid1, ['row1']) == True
    assert v.finish(rid1, ['row1dup']) == False  # duplicate
    # finish with rid2 should succeed
    assert v.finish(rid2, ['row2']) == True
    assert v.rows == ['row2']

def test_loading_and_error():
    v = View()
    v.loading = True
    v.error = 'test error'
    rid = v.begin('q1')
    # begin should clear loading and error
    assert v.loading == False
    assert v.error is None
    # finish with rid should succeed
    assert v.finish(rid, ['row1']) == True
    # after finish, rows updated
    assert v.rows == ['row1']

def test_notes_preserve():
    v = View()
    v.notes['job1'] = 'note1'
    rid = v.begin('q1')
    # finish without touching notes
    v.finish(rid, ['row1'])
    assert v.notes['job1'] == 'note1'
    # another begin/finish
    rid2 = v.begin('q2')
    v.finish(rid2, ['row2'])
    assert v.notes['job1'] == 'note1'

def test_only_latest_begun_updates():
    v = View()
    rid1 = v.begin('q1')
    # simulate a reply for rid1 (should succeed)
    v.finish(rid1, ['row1'])
    # begin another
    rid2 = v.begin('q2')
    # now receive stale reply for rid1 (should fail)
    assert v.finish(rid1, ['stale']) == False
    # finish rid2 succeeds
    assert v.finish(rid2, ['row2']) == True
    assert v.rows == ['row2']

def run_all():
    test_basic()
    test_duplicate_rid()
    test_loading_and_error()
    test_notes_preserve()
    test_only_latest_begun_updates()
    print('All tests passed')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_all()

class View:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = []
        self.notes = {}
        self.loading = False
        self.error = None
        self.seq = 0          # monotonically increasing request id generator
        self._active_id = None  # id of the latest begun request that has not been finished yet
        self._active_finished = False  # True if _active_id has already been successfully finished
    def begin(self, query):
        self.seq += 1
        rid = self.seq
        # clear loading errors but keep existing rows and notes
        self.loading = False
        self.error = None
        # the new active request
        self._active_id = rid
        self._active_finished = False
        return rid
    def finish(self, request_id, rows):
        # only the latest begun request can update rows, once
        if request_id != self._active_id:
            return False
        if self._active_finished:
            # duplicate finish for the same active request
            return False
        # update rows with the valid finish
        self.rows = rows
        self._active_finished = True
        # clear _active_id? No, because a new begin will set a new _active_id.
        # But if we want to allow another begin after finish, the next begin will set a new _active_id.
        # So keep _active_id as is; it will be overwritten by next begin.
        return True
